title: Reviewed findings
description:
Written by `qa-reviewer`. Presence and validity of this file is what the qa-review-gate hook checks; if it is missing or malformed the pipeline stops.

`qa-reviewer` did not propose these findings, so rejecting one costs it nothing. `candidates_digest` binds the review to one specific candidate set, so a review cannot be carried over from a different or stale file.

candidates_digest.description: Digest of findings.candidates.json. Verified by the gate.

reviews.description: Exactly one entry per candidate. The gate rejects the run if any candidate is unreviewed or any review names a candidate that does not exist -- silently dropping an inconvenient candidate is otherwise the path of least resistance.

rationale.description: Why. A minimum length is enforced because 'looks fine' is not a review, and an unenforced minimum reliably produces 'looks fine'.

rejection_reason.description:
Required when verdict is 'rejected'. Enumerated rather than free text so that rejection patterns are analyzable across runs: a reviewer that only ever rejects for 'no_evidence' is not exercising the other axes.

'persona_drift_artifact' means the finding is real but was only reachable by an agent behaving out of character -- a defect a QA engineer would find, which this run was not for.

accepted.description: The findings whose verdict was 'accepted', carried forward in full with any severity/confidence adjustments applied. Redundant with `reviews` on purpose: downstream consumers read one array instead of performing a join, and the gate checks the two agree.
